title: Cell-Wide Survey of Amide-Bonded Lysine Modifications Using Deacetylase CobB
author: Wei, Yang, et al.

steps.title: Prepare required buffers
steps.instruction: Make all buffers fresh on the day of the experiment unless noted otherwise.

substeps.instruction: Binding buffer: dissolve 8.197 g sodium phosphate, 4.383 g NaCl, and 0.681 g imidazole in 400 mL deionized water, adjust pH to 7.2 with HCl, then bring to 500 mL total volume (final: 100 mM Na₂HPO₄, 150 mM NaCl, 20 mM imidazole).

Elution buffer: dissolve 8.197 g sodium phosphate, 4.383 g NaCl, and 10.212 g imidazole in 400 mL deionized water, adjust pH to 7.2 with HCl, then bring to 500 mL total volume (final: 100 mM Na₂HPO₄, 150 mM NaCl, 300 mM imidazole).

Desalination buffer: dissolve 3.029 g Tris base and 4.383 g NaCl in 400 mL deionized water, adjust pH to 7.5 with HCl, then bring to 500 mL total volume (final: 50 mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl). Store up to 1 month at room temperature.
Mitochondria lysis buffer: prepare according to the lab’s standard formulation and keep on ice; supplement with 1× protease inhibitor cocktail before use.

steps.title: Process HCC tissue (optional)
steps.instruction: All steps 2–22 must be performed on ice (4 °C).

substeps.instruction: Dice 2 g of HCC tissue into ~0.1 mm pieces using a razor.
Resuspend tissue pieces in 10 mL ice‑cold (4 °C) homogenization buffer containing 1× protease inhibitor cocktail.
Homogenize with a Dounce homogenizer (≥40 strokes).
Pass the homogenate through a 100‑mm‑diameter cell filter (pore size 125 µm) to remove debris.
Centrifuge filtrate at 1 000×g for 10 min at 4 °C; collect the supernatant (Step 6).
Resuspend the resulting pellet in 10 mL ice‑cold (4 °C) homogenization buffer with 1× protease inhibitor cocktail; vortex.
Centrifuge again at 1 000×g for 10 min at 4 °C; collect the supernatant (Step 8).
Resuspend the new pellet in 2 mL high‑salt buffer; vortex and place on a rotary shaker for 30 min at 4 °C to extract nuclear proteins.
Centrifuge at 1 000×g for 10 min at 4 °C; collect the supernatant (Step 10).
Repeat the high‑salt extraction (steps 9–10) once more and collect the supernatant (Step 11).
Combine the supernatants from Steps 6, 8, 10, and 11 and keep on ice for downstream processing.

steps.title: Process HEK293T cells (optional)
steps.instruction: All steps 13–22 must be performed on ice (4 °C).

substeps.instruction: Harvest two confluent 15‑cm dishes of HEK293T cells by scraping.
Wash cells three times with 10 mL PBS, centrifuging at 1 000×g between washes.
Resuspend the washed cell pellet in 10 mL ice‑cold (4 °C) homogenization buffer containing 1× protease inhibitor cocktail.
Homogenize with a Dounce homogenizer (≥40 strokes).
Centrifuge the homogenate at 1 000×g for 10 min at 4 °C; collect the supernatant (Step 14).
Resuspend the resulting pellet in 10 mL ice‑cold (4 °C) homogenization buffer with protease inhibitor cocktail; vortex.
Centrifuge at 1 000×g for 10 min at 4 °C; collect the supernatant (Step 16).
Repeat the resuspend‑centrifuge cycle (steps 15–16) once more and collect the supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 2 mL high‑salt buffer; vortex and place on a rotary shaker for 30 min at 4 °C to extract nuclear proteins.
Centrifuge at 1 000×g for 10 min at 4 °C; collect the supernatant (Step 19).
Combine the supernatants from Steps 14, 16, 17, and 19 and keep on ice for downstream processing.
Pool the combined supernatants obtained from tissue and/or cell processing.
Centrifuge the pooled extract at 10 000×g for 30 min (room temperature).
Carefully pipette off the supernatant (contains cytosolic and nuclear proteins) and set aside for later steps (go to step 26).
Retain the pellet (contains mitochondria) for mitochondrial protein extraction (go to step 24).

steps.title: Extract mitochondrial proteins
steps.instruction: Lyse mitochondria and collect soluble proteins.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the mitochondrial pellet in 1 mL mitochondria lysis buffer supplemented with 1× protease inhibitor cocktail.
Rotate gently on a rotary shaker for 30 min at 4 °C.
Centrifuge at 12 000×g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant (mitochondrial protein fraction) and discard the remaining pellet.

steps.title: Prepare LC/MS samples
steps.instruction: Convert ADP‑ribose derivatives to butyl esters and reconstitute for injection.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of 3 M HCl in 1‑butanol to each protein sample.
Incubate at 60 °C for 15 min to release metabolites and form butyl esters.
Dry the reaction completely under a stream of nitrogen.
Reconstitute the dried residue with 100 µL injection solvent (80 % water, 20 % methanol, 0.1 % formic acid).

steps.title: Run LC/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 5 µL of each reconstituted sample onto the HPLC system and acquire data using the LC/MS settings described in Table 5.

steps.title: Derivatize for GC/MS
steps.instruction: Convert metabolites to volatile derivatives suitable for GC/MS.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of pyridine solution containing 250 mM methoxyamine hydrochloride to each dried sample.
Incubate at 70 °C for 90 min with shaking (handle in a fume hood; reagents are toxic).
Add 100 µL of MTBSTFA (20 % in pyridine) to the reaction mixture.
Incubate at 30 °C for 60 min with shaking (MTBSTFA is toxic; handle with care).

steps.title: Prepare GC/MS samples
steps.instruction: Filter and transfer derivatized metabolites for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Filter each derivatized reaction through a 0.22‑µm syringe‑driven filter; collect the filtrate.
Transfer 100 µL of the filtrate into GC vials.
Analyze the derivatized metabolites as soon as possible; if storage is required, keep at –80 °C (stability ranges from days to months).

steps.title: Run GC/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Perform GC/MS using the instrument settings listed in Table 6 and acquire spectra for each sample.

steps.title: Process peak data
steps.instruction: Export, normalize, and compare chromatographic peaks.

substeps.instruction: Export GC or LC peak areas for each sample as CSV tables (steps 43 or 48).
Normalize all peak areas to the internal control adonitol area.
Compare peak areas of CobB‑treated samples with matched untreated controls; record metabolites showing ≥3‑fold increase as positive hits.

steps.title: Identify metabolites
steps.instruction: Obtain MS/MS spectra of positive hits and search spectral libraries.

substeps.instruction: Acquire MS/MS spectra for each candidate metabolite.
Search the spectra against the NIST mass spectral library to assign metabolite identities.

steps.title: Quantify targeted lysine modifications
steps.instruction: Use synthetic peptide calibrators to determine modification levels.

substeps.instruction: Synthesize peptides containing the lysine modifications of interest; verify purity >98 %.
Spike known concentrations of each synthetic peptide into the protein samples.
Run the spiked samples through the entire workflow (steps 1–54).
Compare the GC or LC peak areas of the targeted modifiers in spiked versus unspiked samples.
Calculate modification levels in the original samples by reference to the internal peptide calibrators.
Optionally, generate a working curve by analyzing a series of peptide concentrations and use it to quantify unknown samples.
